prereg.threshold: 0.05 absolute; pooled SD per the program-wide statistical conventions, i.e. sqrt((s1^2+s2^2)/2)

Q1_decision_rules.i: B1 DROPS by > 0.05 while V2b holds within 0.05 => B1's robustness IS chemistry-specific; the memorization story PARTIALLY REVIVES for geometric OOD; report both splits side by side
Q1_decision_rules.ii: B1 HOLDS within 0.05 => B1's robustness is GENERAL across both OOD axes; the memorization story is closed as refuted and exclusion_baselines branch (a) is strengthened on a properly powered test
Q1_decision_rules.iii: BOTH arms drop > 0.05 => difficulty shift again; compare ORDERING only and state that a balanced geometric-OOD split is simply harder (this being a TRAINED comparison, a joint drop is informative about task difficulty, not contamination)
Q1_decision_rules.in_all_cases: report each arm against the external_baselines regularity floor 0.5286, not only against chance — an arm below the floor has not demonstrated crystallographic reasoning

Q2_decision_rules.i: an arm IMPROVES by > 0.05 at native => resolution WAS a real constraint; resolution_audit's B1 drop was train/test mismatch; annotate all prior perception results as resolution-limited
Q2_decision_rules.ii: accuracies FLAT within 0.05 for both arms => resolution was NOT a constraint at this render size; resolution_audit's 'resolution excluded' becomes defensible and the 416-eff results stand as-is
Q2_decision_rules.iii: an arm DEGRADES by > 0.05 at native even when trained natively => genuine and surprising; investigate before asserting a mechanism
Q2_decision_rules.secondary: geometry-STEP accuracy for V2b native-trained vs the 0.6349 / 0.6476 pair from resolution_audit item 2. If the natively-trained geometry step still fails to beat the 416 value by > 0.05, the fabrication diagnosis is confirmed under the strongest available test and the 'responsive to the image without being informed by it' sentence stands; if it DOES improve, that sentence must be weakened to apply only to 416-trained models

confounds_fixed_in_advance: Q1 and Q2 are entangled BY DESIGN in this run (new split AND new resolution); acceptable only because 416-eff/composition-exclusion references exist for both arms, so each comparison changes one axis relative to a known reference. It is NOT a clean 2x2 and must not be described as one. A full factorial (2 splits x 2 resolutions x 3 seeds) is 4x the cost and is explicitly NOT being run

data/geometry_sft eval is 93.8% contained in data/primary's TRAIN set — irrelevant here because training is on data/geometry_sft/train, disjoint from data/geometry_sft/eval by construction (0 prototype overlap, verified), but these checkpoints must NEVER be evaluated on data/primary's eval set and the 416-eff references must never be recomputed from them

prereg.uninformative_condition: if both arms land below the regularity floor 0.5286 on the balanced geometric-OOD eval, neither arm demonstrated crystallographic reasoning and both Q1 and Q2 become unanswerable from it — report that plainly rather than interpreting sub-floor differences

S5_B1_416_comp1610.observation_recorded_in_advance: a final training loss of 0.0064 on 1610 examples indicates the model has essentially MEMORISED the training targets. For the B1 arm the target is a single crystal-system word, so near-zero training loss is expected and is NOT by itself evidence of overfitting to the eval. But Q3 (scale 115 -> 1610) then compares two REGIMES that have both saturated their training objective, and any Q3 difference must be attributed to what the larger sample TAUGHT rather than to longer optimisation
